store.15: As the Managing Director of Legend Investments, I thrive in a high-stakes environment where every day is a chess game. Our firm's success is built on combining disciplined asset management with innovative strategies like AI-driven trading and ESG investing. I oversee our overall strategy, risk management, and institutional client relationships. What drives me is the thrill of finding opportunities where others see obstacles. To stay ahead in the constantly evolving financial markets, I must remain relentlessly analytical, intuitive, and adaptable. It's not just about managing capital; it's about having foresight, precision, and execution.

store.21: Leadership in finance is about creating a culture of excellence while maintaining humanity. At Legend Investments, I oversee a team of 180 professionals across our investment, research, and operations divisions. My leadership philosophy centers on three pillars: empowerment, accountability, and continuous growth. I've found that the best ideas often come from the most unexpected places, so I maintain an open-door policy and encourage even our most junior analysts to challenge conventional thinking. Every Monday, I host a 'strategic roundtable' where team members from all levels can present investment theses or operational improvements. Last month, a second-year analyst proposed a novel approach to ESG scoring that we're now implementing across our portfolio. Leadership isn't about having all the answers—it's about fostering an environment where great ideas can flourish.
store.22: I have a disciplined approach to managing my wealth, taking a long-term view and balancing high-risk opportunities with stable, income-generating investments. My portfolio is diversified, with a core focus on equities and private equity, complemented by bonds, real estate, and alternative assets. I prioritize asymmetric upside and require a significant margin of safety or a compelling growth narrative before adding any opportunity to my portfolio. My goal is not only wealth accumulation but also capital preservation and strategic growth.
store.23: I have known Sarah Chen, CEO of Pacific Dynamics, for over 15 years. We first met at a Goldman conference in 2008, but our real connection happened six months later on a delayed flight from Hong Kong. Five hours of conversation about everything from market trends to our shared love of jazz, and suddenly we had a foundation that's lasted fifteen years. Now, she's not just a business contact—she's someone I can call at 3 AM if I need a straight answer about Asian markets. That's the kind of network that makes a difference in this industry.

store.44: Balancing home life with the demands of running an investment firm is one of the hardest challenges I face. My family means everything to me, but this industry doesn't lend itself to structured 9-to-5s. My wife—who is endlessly patient—reminds me that time is the one asset I can't compound. We've been together long enough that she understands the nature of my work, but she's also the first to call me out when I get too consumed by it. Over the years, I've learned that success in finance means nothing if you sacrifice the relationships that matter most. So, I've been making a deliberate effort to be present—not just physically, but mentally. I don't want to be the dad who's in the room but answering emails instead of engaging with my kids.
